newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-SIDHU AND DRAVID FRUSTRATE WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIDHU AND DRAVID FRUSTRATE WEST INDIES.

text.p: Navjot Sidhu and Rahul Dravid frustrated West Indies with a half-century second wicket partnership on the second day of the second test on Saturday.
Replying to West Indies' first innings 296, India were 77 for one at tea after losing a wicket in the first over of their innings. Sidhu was unbeaten on 51 while Dravid had scored 21.
Earlier Barbadian Roland Holder fell short of a maiden test century by nine runs as West Indies, resuming at 239 for seven, lost their last three wickets for just seven runs.
Holder was bowled leg stump by left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi after a 239-ball innings lasting 293 minutes with seven fours.
Leg-spinner Anil Kumble was the most successful of the Indian bowlers with five for 104 off 38 overs.
Curtly Ambrose struck with the second ball of the Indian innings, trapping Vangipurappu Laxman lbw for a duck when the batsman played back to a full delivery.
